# Problem 1

### Write birthday function

```{r}
bday_sim = function(n) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)
  repeated_bday = n_distinct(birthdays) < n
  repeated_bday
}
```

### Run it 10000 times for each group size between 2 and 50

```{r}
bday_sim_df =
  expand_grid(group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000) |>
  mutate(shared_bday = map_lgl(group_size, bday_sim)) |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(prob_shared = mean(shared_bday)
)
```


### Plot

```{r}
bday_sim_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = prob_shared)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Probability that at least two people share a birthday",
    x = "Group size",
    y = "Estimated probability")
```

The probability of shared birthdays increases with group size. It is near 0 for small groups, passes 50% at a group size of about 23, and is close to 1 for a group of 50. 


# Problem 2

### Data frame of file names

```{r}
study_df =
  tibble(file_name = list.files("./data")
  )
```

### Read every file

```{r message = FALSE}
study_df =
  tibble(file_name = list.files("./data")
  ) |>
  mutate(file_path = str_c("./data/", file_name),
    data = map(file_path, read_csv)
  )
```

### Tidy the data

```{r message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
study_df = tibble(
    file_name = list.files("./data")
  ) |>
  mutate( file_path = str_c("./data/", file_name),
    data = map(file_path, read_csv)
  ) |>
  unnest(data) |>
  mutate(file_name = str_replace(file_name, ".csv", "")) |>
  separate(file_name, into = c("arm", "subject_id"), sep = "_") |>
  mutate(
    arm = case_match(arm, "con" ~ "Control", "exp" ~ "Experimental"),
    subject = str_c(arm, " ", subject_id)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    week_1:week_8,
    names_to = "week",
    names_prefix = "week_",
    values_to = "observation"
  ) |>
  mutate(week = as.numeric(week)) |>
  select(subject, arm, subject_id, week, observation)
```

### Spaghetti plot

```{r}
study_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = observation, group = subject, color = arm)) +
  geom_line(alpha = .7) +
  geom_point(alpha = .7, size = .8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8) +
  labs(
    title = "Observations over time for each subject",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Observation",
    color = "Study arm")
```

At the start of the study, the two groups have similar observations. Over the eight weeks, observations in the experimental arm increase steadily, while observations in the control arm stay roughly flat. By the end of the study, every experimental subject has a higher observation than every control subject, suggesting the intervention is associated with an increase in the outcome over time.

# Problem 3

### Function for one dataset and one test

```{r ttest_function}
sim_ttest = function(mu, n = 30, sigma = 5) {
  sim_data = tibble(x = rnorm(n, mean = mu, sd = sigma)
  )
  t.test(pull(sim_data, x), mu = 0) |>
    broom::tidy() |>
    select(estimate, p.value)
}
```

### Run 5000 datasets for each

```{r}
power_sim_df =
  expand_grid(
    true_mu = 0:6,
    iter = 1:5000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    estimate_df = map(true_mu, sim_ttest)
  ) |>
  unnest(estimate_df)
```

### Power plot

```{r}
power_sim_df |>
  group_by(true_mu) |>
  summarize(power = mean(p.value < 0.05)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = true_mu, y = power)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  labs(
    title = "Power of a one-sample t-test (n = 30, σ = 5)",
    x = "True value of μ",
    y = "Power (proportion of nulls rejected)")
```
